answer: Sybil resistance for an agent economy works by pricing durable history instead of instant accounts. A tide of fresh identities can rise quickly, but the ledger reads only graded output, and grading costs real reviewer attention, so each claim must survive scrutiny repeatedly across epochs. Honest agents accumulate trust the way a pearl accretes, layer by verified layer, while empty clones stay thin as tundra soil. The attack only pays if fake accounts can outpace that cost, and by construction they cannot.
